sections.html:
Lehi sits at the northern end of Utah Valley in Utah County, a few miles from the Provo-Orem area. It stayed small for a century, with a census low of 2,733 in 1940 and only 8,475 in 1990, then took off: 19,028 in 2000, 47,407 in 2010 and 75,907 in 2020, with an estimate of 95,313 for July 2025. The 2020 median age was 26.2, and about 39.5 percent of residents were under 18.

Family-sized homes are the norm. An older house in the original grid can look very different from a subdivision built a few years ago, so condition and age drive how buyers compare them.

Many owners here bought during a tech hiring wave. A layoff, a remote work shift or a job offer elsewhere can force a move, and the main challenge then is timing, since the mortgage payment continues while the house waits for a buyer.

Interstate 15 runs through Lehi with five exits, which is a main reason many households choose the city. FrontRunner commuter rail opened its Lehi station near Thanksgiving Point on December 12, 2012, and Utah Transit Authority runs local buses. Distance to an I-15 ramp or the station is something a buyer's agent will price in, so a house far from the interstate may attract a different buyer than one near the Corporate Center on Traverse Mountain.

sections.h2: Schools and the coming district split
sections.html: Lehi public schools, including Lehi High and Skyridge High, have been run by the Alpine School District. That district will cease to exist in July 2027 and be replaced by three new districts, one of them named Aspen Peaks. Confirm the future district for the exact property with the district or the city before you promise a buyer anything about schools.

Lehi's Building and Inspections Department issues all building permits, and any open permit or unfinished work can delay a closing. Applications go through an online submittal portal, and current codes include the 2021 I-Codes and the 2020 National Electrical Code with Utah amendments.

  • Call 385-201-1035 to schedule an inspection, with at least 24 hours notice. Voicemail, email and online requests do not book one.
  • Have the work ready first, because re-inspection fees apply when a project clearly is not.
  • Look up status by permit number, site address or subdivision and lot.

Lehi City is at 131 N 100 E, phone (385) 201-1000.

Lehi runs a pressurized irrigation system that supplies untreated water for yards and city fire hydrants. A city ordinance prohibits irrigation water use after October 15, owners turn the connection on and off each year, and the city is currently in Phase 2 of its Water Shortage Management Plan. Buyers from elsewhere often ask how the yard is watered, so explain the connection and watering schedule up front.

sections.h2: Valuation notices, tax bills and recording
sections.html:
Utah County mails valuation notices in the summer, sends tax notices in October and collects taxes by 5:00 pm on November 30. Appeals go to the Utah County Board of Equalization through the Auditor at 111 S. University Ave, Provo, or by phone at (801) 851-8109, option 3. The deadline in a typical year is September 15, and the date printed on your notice governs.

The valuation notice is not a bill. Amounts due appear in the October tax notice, so a seller closing in the fall should ask the title company how that year's taxes are being prorated.

Deeds are recorded with the Utah County Recorder, and the fee has been $40 per document. County recording fees can change, so ask the recorder for the current figure before closing.

sections.h2: Does the primary residence exemption follow the house?
sections.html:
No, the exemption does not transfer. Utah removes 45 percent of the market value of a primary home, so taxable value is 55 percent, and the owner must live in the home at least 183 consecutive days in a calendar year.

After a sale or deed transfer, the new owner files Form TC-473A with the county Board of Equalization by September 15, and counties cannot take late filings. A buyer who misses the date can be taxed on the full market value for that year. Owners of rentals file a residential declaration signed by all owners instead, and second or vacation homes do not qualify.

Telling a buyer about that deadline in advance avoids a surprise tax bill after a fall closing.

sections.h2: Selling with open permits or liens
sections.html:
Open permits are the most common snag in a fast closing. If a finished basement, a deck or a remodel never got its final inspection, the title company or a lender may ask for it to be closed out, which means a call to 385-201-1035 and a day of notice. A cash buyer can often take the house as it stands, but the item still shows up in the paperwork, so find out what is open before anything is signed.

Liens are handled at the table. The title search lists unpaid taxes, a mortgage payoff or any judgment against the property, and each one is paid from your proceeds before you receive the balance. Ask for the figures ahead of signing day so the final number is no surprise.

sections.h2: What to gather before you call
sections.html: Pull the deed, your latest tax notice, any permit records for finished space and a recent mortgage statement. If the yard uses pressurized irrigation, note when the connection is turned on each year. If the house came to you through an estate, add the court papers that show who may sign. With those documents in hand, a buyer can price the house in one conversation and the title company can start its search right away.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works for a Lehi house
sections.html:
A cash sale uses the same title and recording steps, without lender approval. A title company searches for liens, the parties sign, and the deed is recorded in Provo.

  1. Tell the buyer about the house, its condition and your timeline.
  2. Compare the offer and closing date with a listing plan.
  3. Clear any open permits or liens before the closing date.
  4. Sign and receive the proceeds after payoffs and prorated taxes.

That path suits owners who inherited a Lehi house, are behind on payments, or have a house that needs work they do not want to finance. There are no showings and no repair negotiations, and the closing date is set with you. You also skip the wait for a buyer's loan, which in a fast-moving market is often the step that falls through late.

faqs.q: How many people live in Lehi, Utah?
faqs.a: About 95,313 as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 75,907, up from 47,407 in 2010.

faqs.q: When are Utah County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By 5:00 pm on November 30. Utah County mails tax notices in October, and a valuation notice is not a bill.

faqs.q: What is the Utah County appeal deadline for a Lehi property valuation?
faqs.a: September 15 in a typical year. Check the notice you receive, since the date printed on it governs.

faqs.q: Will Alpine School District still serve Lehi?
faqs.a: Not after July 2027. Alpine School District will be replaced by three new districts, so confirm the district for a specific address before telling buyers.

faqs.q: Who inspects building work in Lehi?
faqs.a: The city's Building and Inspections Department. Call 385-201-1035 at least 24 hours ahead to schedule an inspection.
